newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale has not ruled out CWB barley vote.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale has not ruled out CWB barley vote.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale has not ruled out the possibility of asking 130,000 Prairie farmers to vote on whether the Canadian Wheat Board should retain its export monopoly on feed and malt barley, an Agriculture Canada spokesman said.
"He (Goodale) hasn't ruled the idea out," Goodale spokesman Vern Greenshields said in a telephone interview.
Goodale will announce his decision on an independent review of changes to the CWB in his electoral constituency of Regina, Saskatchewan, at 1200 EDT/1600 GMT Friday.
A panel appointed by Goodale last December to study the contentious issue of grain and oilseed marketing recommended removing feed barley from the CWB.

"I've heard farmers will be asked if the (Canadian Wheat) Board should lose all barley exports (in its monopoly mandate) or not, including malting barley, as a way to force a 'no' vote," one source said.
A government-commissioned poll of farmers done in August found producers almost evenly divided on the barley issue.
Goodale will likely announce a Prairie-wide plebiscite to break the impasse, industry sources said.
The 61-year-old state commodity trading monopoly held a 48 percent share of the world malt barley market in crop year 1994/95 (Aug/July). It held an 11 percent share of the world feed barley market.
Most Canadian malt barley is exported but two thirds of feed barley is sold domestically.
The CWB estimated two-row malting barley prices last week at C$245-225 a tonne, six-row malting barley at C$205-185 and top grade feed barley at C$170-150 a tonne.
